## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design an end-to-end automated DR with data-plane concerns, cross-region replication, data freshness, policy guardrails, and FIS orchestration.

## Key Concepts
- AWS FIS for controlled chaos experiments
- Cross-region data replication and artifact consistency (S3, SageMaker)
- Route 53 failover and service mesh traffic routing
- End-to-end SLIs: latency, error rate, data freshness
- Policy guardrails: OPA Gatekeeper, IAM Roles Anywhere

## Code Example
```yaml
# Pseudo-FIS experiment outline
experimentTemplate:
  description: DR exercise for two-region deployment
  targets:
    regionA: {resourceType: aws:region, selectionMode: all}
    regionB: {resourceType: aws:region, selectionMode: all}
  actions:
    - name: RouteTrafficToB
      action: aws:route53:recordSet
      parameters:
        type: A
        setIdentifier: region-b-weighted
        weight: 100
    - name: PauseReplication
      action: aws:dms:pauseReplication
      parameters:
        targetEndpoint: data-lake
  startAfter: 0
  duration: 600s
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you throttle cutover to minimize user impact?
- What metrics or guards would you add to ensure safe rollback in case of partial failures?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design risk-controlled feature flags in a serverless setup, plus automated testing and rollback integration.

## Key Concepts
- AWS AppConfig for feature flags
- CodePipeline and CodeBuild integration
- CloudFormation IaC for infrastructure
- Rollout percentages and automatic rollback

## Code Example
```yaml
# CloudFormation snippet (partial)
Resources:
  AppConfigApplication:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Application
    Properties:
      Name: ServerlessApiApp

  AppConfigEnvironment:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Environment
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      Name: Production

  AppConfigConfigurationProfile:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::ConfigurationProfile
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      Name: FeatureFlags
      LocationUri: hosted

  AppConfigHostedConfigurationVersion:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::HostedConfigurationVersion
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      ConfigurationProfileId: !Ref AppConfigConfigurationProfile
      Content: '{"search-v2-enabled": {"value": false, "enabled": true, "type": "Boolean"}}'
      ContentType: application/json

  AppConfigDeployment:
    Type: AWS::AppConfig::Deployment
    Properties:
      ApplicationId: !Ref AppConfigApplication
      ConfigurationProfileId: !Ref AppConfigConfigurationProfile
      ConfigurationVersion: !Ref AppConfigHostedConfigurationVersion
      Environment: !Ref AppConfigEnvironment
      DeploymentStrategy: Rolling_10PercentEvery10Minutes
```

## Testing Steps
1. Deploy CloudFormation stack to create AppConfig resources
2. Update Lambda function to read the feature flag from AppConfig
3. Configure CodeBuild stage in CodePipeline to:
   - Query AppConfig for flag status
   - Run smoke tests against /search-v2 when flag is enabled
   - Fail the build if tests fail (triggers pipeline rollback)
4. Set initial rollout to 10% in AppConfig deployment strategy
5. Monitor metrics and gradually increase rollout percentage
6. On complete rollout, update flag to 100% or remove the flag entirely

Resources:

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes cost-aware, cross-region preview management, tying spend controls to operational gates and rollback readiness. It tests practical implementation details across GitHub Actions, AWS Budgets, and automatic teardown.

## Key Concepts
- Cost governance with per-resource tagging and AWS Budgets
- Ephemeral, multi-region preview environments in EKS
- Idle-resource detection and automated teardown
- Health gates and automated rollback pathways
- Observability and alerting for budget and health events

## Code Example
```yaml
name: cost-aware-preview
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
jobs:
  deploy-preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: provision preview
        run: |
          # deploy preview namespaces/clusters via CDK
          npm run cdk deploy PreviewStack -- -c pr_id=${{ github.head_ref }}
      - name: enforce budget tag
        run: |
          # tag resources with pr_id for budgeting
          ./scripts/tag-preview.sh pr_id=${{ github.head_ref }}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate the idle-detection window across regions?
- What changes would you make to handle PR closures vs. merges in budgeting?
